title: The duration of the unfair game

prereqs.why: The identity is what turns the known final wealth into the expected number of games.
The ruin probability from the previous problem is the input this one needs.
Wald needs the number of games to be a stopping time with finite mean, and both have to be checked.

statement:
Continue the game of the previous problem: $\pounds1$ stakes, win
probability $p = \tfrac25$, start at $k = 3$, barriers at $0$ and $m = 6$. Let
$T$ be the number of games played. It is a stopping time with $\E T < \infty$.

Write $S_T$ for the final wealth. You already know
$h_3 = \P(S_T = 6) = \tfrac{8}{35}$, so

$$\E S_T = 6 h_3 + 0\,(1 - h_3) = \tfrac{48}{35}.$$

Wald's identity applied to the steps $X_1, X_2, \dots$ (each with mean
$p - q$) gives

$$\E S_T = k + \E(X_1)\,\E T = 3 + (p-q)\,\E T .$$

Give $\E T$ exactly.
hints: Work out $p - q$ first. It is negative, which it has to be — an unfavourable game drifts downwards.
Set the two expressions for $\E S_T$ equal and solve the linear equation for $\E T$.
$\tfrac{48}{35} = 3 - \tfrac15 \E T$. Put the right-hand side over 35 before rearranging.
Both sides being rearranged, $\tfrac15 \E T = 3 - \tfrac{48}{35}$. Expect an answer between 8 and 9.

payload.prompt: The expected number of games played.
payload.label: $\E T =$
payload.syntax: A number or a fraction. Arithmetic is fine.
